issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument messageOnRide() method that returns a String (e.g., the template's Main calls r.messageOnRide() and the spec describes messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). However, the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and corresponding implementations in Pig and Seal take an int parameter). This parameter mismatch between the specified/interface usage and the solution will confuse students and prevents direct use of the template's example code or the implementation they are asked to provide.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and all implementations consistent with the problem statement and template. Either (A) change the solution to define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters (String messageOnRide()) and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg version returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require a parameter (e.g., int speed) and adjust the specification text and example calls accordingly. Prefer fixing the solution to use the no-arg signature to match the exercise description and template Main usage.

issues.description: The problem specification and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning a String (UML and example usage), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements Pig/Seal with the int parameter and a different return format (includes speed). This changes the method signature and expected behavior across artifacts, causing students to be unable to map the required interface method from the problem/template to the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations match the problem/template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide() : String in the solution (update Rideable.java, Pig.java, Seal.java) and have implementations return exactly 'Riding on [Animal Type] [name]'. Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust example usages accordingly.
